# Contest contract

Six new problems mix condensation degrees, Euler reconstruction, bridge theorems, block-cut paths, and dominator sets. Suggested order: A, D, B, C, E, F.

| Problem | Main invariant |
|---|---|
| A | the only possible universal destination is the unique sink SCC |
| B | every source and sink SCC needs a new incident direction |
| C | words are labeled directed edges consumed by Hierholzer |
| D | Robbins' theorem: a connected undirected graph is strongly orientable iff it has no bridge |
| E | failed-vertex connectivity is the negation of block-cut path membership |
| F | a vertex dominates exactly the targets whose dominator set contains it |

# Recognition and discovery

| Quantifier or operation | Compression |
|---|---|
| reachable from every vertex | unique sink SCC |
| add edges for strong connectivity | source/sink SCC counts |
| use every labeled transition once | Euler trail |
| strongly orient every undirected edge | bridges and Robbins |
| connectivity after one failure | block-cut path |
| lies on every directed root path | dominators |

After SCC contraction, every source needs new indegree and every sink needs new
outdegree, giving `max(sources,sinks)` additions unless there is one SCC.
For Robbins orientation, a bridge makes strong orientation impossible;
without bridges, downward tree edges and upward back edges let every DFS
subtree travel both ways.

Undirected “every path” becomes articulation membership in a block-cut tree.
Directed rooted “every path” becomes domination. Tiny oracles should use
transitive closure, enumerate orientations, delete failed vertices followed by
BFS, and enumerate simple root-to-target paths.

# Exercises

Problems A--F form the complete mixed contest.
